source.text: פַּלְגֵי־מַ֣יִם לֶב־מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Channels of water [is the] heart of a king in [the] hand of YHWH; to all that he desires he turns it.

en.L: [Like] channels of water [is the] heart of a king in [the] hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turns it wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} desires.
en.B: A king's heart is like streams of water in the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q who directs it wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} pleases.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} guides a king's thoughts the way a farmer guides water along a ditch. \q He turns the king's heart wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

fr.L: [Comme] des canaux d’eau [est le] cœur du roi dans [la] main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le dirige partout où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} veut.
fr.B: Le cœur du roi est comme des ruisseaux dans la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q qui l’oriente là où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le veut.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} guide les pensées d’un roi comme un paysan guide l’eau dans un fossé. \q Il oriente le cœur du roi là où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} veut.

decisions.choice: channels of water: irrigation channels that are steered where they are needed
decisions.reason: The word (peleg) is a channel or watercourse (5:16; Psalm 1:3). As a farmer cuts the channel to lead the water, the LORD leads even the most powerful human will.

decisions.choice: God's rule over rulers
decisions.reason: Even a king, whose word decides for others (16:10; 20:8), is not outside God's control (16:1, 9; Ezra 7:27).

decisions.choice: the way a farmer guides water along a ditch
decisions.reason: Readable names the farmer to make the irrigation picture plain.

source.text: כָּֽל־דֶּרֶךְ־אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Every way of a person [is] upright in his eyes, and YHWH weighs hearts.

en.L: Every way of a person [is] right in {{gender:their|his}} own eyes, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} weighs [the] hearts.
en.B: People think every road they take is right, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} weighs the heart.
en.R: People always believe that what they do is right. \q But {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sees what is really in their hearts.

fr.L: Toute voie de l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} [est] droite à ses propres yeux, \q mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pèse [les] cœurs.
fr.B: Les humains pensent que chaque route qu’ils prennent est la bonne, \q mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pèse le cœur.
fr.R: Les gens croient toujours que ce qu’ils font est bien. \q Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} voit ce qu’il y a vraiment dans leur cœur.

decisions.choice: weighs hearts: tests motives, as in 16:2
decisions.reason: Nearly the same saying stands in 16:2, with "spirits" for "hearts" and "pure" for "right"; compare 12:15 and 24:12.

source.text: עֲ֭שֹׂה צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נִבְחָ֖ר לַיהוָ֣ה מִזָּֽבַח׃

records.literal_gloss: To do righteousness and justice [is] chosen by YHWH more than sacrifice.

en.L: To do righteousness and justice \q [is] preferred by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} more than sacrifice.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} would rather see people do what is right and just \q than offer sacrifice.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} wants people to do what is right and fair. \q That matters more to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} than offering sacrifices.

fr.L: Pratiquer la justice et le droit \q [est] préféré par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au sacrifice.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} aime mieux voir les gens faire ce qui est juste et droit \q qu’offrir des sacrifices.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} veut que les gens fassent ce qui est bien et juste. \q Cela compte plus pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que d’offrir des sacrifices.

decisions.choice: right living over ritual
decisions.reason: The prophets say the same (1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6; Micah 6:6–8). Sacrifice is not rejected; it is worthless without justice (verse 27; 15:8).

source.text: רוּם־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַב־לֵ֑ב נִ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: Haughtiness of eyes and wideness of heart, [the] lamp of [the] wicked, [is] sin.

en.L: Haughty eyes and a swollen heart, \q [the] lamp of [the] wicked, [are] sin.
en.B: Proud eyes and an arrogant heart, \q the lamp that lights the way of the wicked, are sin.
en.R: Proud looks and a proud heart are sin. \q Yet that pride is the light wicked people live by.

fr.L: Yeux hautains et cœur enflé, \q [la] lampe des méchants, [c’est] le péché.
fr.B: Les regards orgueilleux et le cœur arrogant, \q cette lampe qui éclaire le chemin des méchants, sont péché.
fr.R: Les regards fiers et le cœur orgueilleux sont un péché. \q Pourtant, c’est cet orgueil qui guide la vie des méchants.

decisions.choice: haughty eyes and a wide heart: pride and arrogance
decisions.reason: Raised eyes are pride (6:17; 30:13); a wide heart is an inflated, arrogant mind (Psalm 101:5).

decisions.choice: lamp (ner): what guides or marks the wicked
alternatives: the plowed ground of the wicked (nir): what they produce
decisions.reason: The consonants can be read as "lamp" (as the vowels have it, compare 13:9; 20:27) or as "newly plowed ground" (nir, 13:23; Jeremiah 4:3), that is, the crop the wicked produce. Either way, their pride and all it yields is sin.

source.text: מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת חָ֭רוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָ֑ר וְכָל־אָ֝֗ץ אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] plans of a diligent [person are] only to profit, and every [one who] hastens [is] only to lack.

en.L: [The] plans of [the] diligent [lead] only to profit, \q but everyone who hurries [comes] only to want.
en.B: The plans of the diligent bring nothing but gain, \q but all who rush in haste come to nothing but need.
en.R: Hard workers who plan carefully will have plenty. \q People who rush into things end up poor.

fr.L: [Les] projets du diligent [mènent] seulement au profit, \q mais quiconque se précipite [va] seulement à la disette.
fr.B: Les projets des gens appliqués n’apportent que du gain, \q mais tous ceux qui se précipitent n’arrivent qu’au manque.
fr.R: Ceux qui travaillent dur et prévoient bien auront assez. \q Ceux qui se précipitent finissent pauvres.

decisions.choice: diligent against hasty: careful effort against rash shortcuts
decisions.reason: The diligent (harus) appear in 10:4 and 13:4. The one who hurries acts without thought or grabs for quick gain (19:2; 28:20). The double "only" (ak) sets the two outcomes side by side.

source.text: פֹּ֣עַל א֭וֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר הֶ֥בֶל נִ֝דָּ֗ף מְבַקְשֵׁי־מָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] acquisition of treasures by a tongue of falsehood [is] a breath driven about, seekers of death.

en.L: Getting treasures by a lying tongue [is] a vapor blown away; \q [they are] seekers of death.
en.B: Riches gained by a lying tongue are a mist that drifts away, \q and those who seek them seek death.
en.R: Money gained by lying vanishes like a breath on the wind. \q People who get rich that way are heading toward death.

fr.L: Acquérir des trésors par une langue mensongère [est] une vapeur emportée ; \q [ce sont des] chercheurs de mort.
fr.B: Les richesses gagnées par une langue menteuse sont une brume qui se dissipe, \q et ceux qui les recherchent cherchent la mort.
fr.R: L’argent gagné en mentant disparaît comme un souffle dans le vent. \q Ceux qui s’enrichissent ainsi vont vers la mort.

decisions.choice: a vapor blown away: gain that vanishes
decisions.reason: Breath (hevel) is what does not last (13:11; Ecclesiastes 1:2); driven about, it is soon gone.

decisions.choice: seekers of death
alternatives: snares of death (Greek and some Hebrew manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text reads "seekers of death": those who gain this way are pursuing their own death (8:36). The Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts read "snares of death" (with a slightly different word, compare 13:14; 14:27), which makes the riches a deadly trap.

source.text: שֹׁד־רְשָׁעִ֥ים יְגוֹרֵ֑ם כִּ֥י מֵ֝אֲנ֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] violence of [the] wicked will drag them away, because they refuse to do justice.

en.L: [The] violence of [the] wicked will drag them away, \q because they refuse to do justice.
en.B: The wicked are swept away by their own violence, \q since they will not do what is just.
en.R: Wicked people will be destroyed by their own violence, \q because they will not do what is right.

fr.L: [La] violence des méchants les entraînera, \q parce qu’ils refusent de pratiquer le droit.
fr.B: Les méchants sont emportés par leur propre violence, \q puisqu’ils refusent de faire ce qui est juste.
fr.R: Les méchants seront détruits par leur propre violence, \q parce qu’ils ne veulent pas faire ce qui est juste.

decisions.choice: drag them away: their violence catches them like a net
decisions.reason: The verb (garar) is used of dragging fish in a net (Habakkuk 1:15). Violence turns back on those who use it (1:18–19).

source.text: הֲפַכְפַּ֬ךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ וָזָ֑ר וְ֝זַ֗ךְ יָשָׁ֥ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Very crooked [is the] way of a person guilty, and [the] pure, upright [is] his work.

en.L: [The] way of a guilty person [is] crooked, \q but [as for the] pure, {{gender:their|his}} conduct [is] upright.
en.B: The path of the guilty is twisted, \q but the conduct of the pure is straight.
en.R: Guilty people live crooked lives. \q But people who are pure in heart do what is right.

fr.L: [La] voie de l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} coupable [est] tortueuse, \q mais [quant à celui qui est] pur, sa conduite [est] droite.
fr.B: Le chemin du coupable est tordu, \q mais la conduite de celui qui est pur est droite.
fr.R: Les coupables vivent de travers. \q Mais ceux qui ont le cœur pur font ce qui est juste.

decisions.choice: crooked ... guilty: twisted ways of one laden with guilt
alternatives: the way of a person is crooked and strange
decisions.reason: Crooked (hafakpak) is a doubled form, "very twisted". The next word (wazar) appears only here; it is usually taken as "guilty" (from a word known in Arabic), but it can be divided as "and strange", giving "a person's way is twisted and strange".

source.text: ט֗וֹב לָשֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Good to dwell on a corner of a roof more than a woman of contentions and a house of association.

en.L: [It is] better to live on a corner of [the] roof \q than [with] a woman of quarrels in a shared house.
en.B: It is better to live up in a corner of the rooftop \q than to share a home with a wife who quarrels.
en.R: It is better to live alone in a corner of a flat roof \q than to share a house with a wife who is always arguing.

fr.L: Mieux vaut habiter à un coin du toit \q qu’[avec] une femme querelleuse dans une maison commune.
fr.B: Mieux vaut vivre dans un coin, en haut sur le toit, \q que partager la maison d’une épouse querelleuse.
fr.R: Il vaut mieux vivre seul dans un coin d’un toit plat \q que partager une maison avec une femme qui se dispute tout le temps.

decisions.choice: a corner of the roof: a cramped, exposed spot on a flat roof
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs used for work and sleep (Joshua 2:6; 1 Samuel 9:25). A corner up there is open to sun and rain, yet better than constant quarrels below. The saying is repeated in 25:24; compare verse 19 and 19:13.

decisions.choice: a house of association: a house shared with her
decisions.reason: The phrase (bet haver) means a house held in common. Some take it as a large or busy house, but sharing fits the contrast with living alone on the roof.

source.text: נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָ֭שָׁע אִוְּתָה־רָ֑ע לֹא־יֻחַ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֣יו רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] appetite of a wicked [person] craves evil; his neighbor is not shown favor in his eyes.

en.L: [The] soul of [the] wicked craves evil; \q {{gender:their|his}} neighbor finds no favor in {{gender:their|his}} eyes.
en.B: The wicked hunger for evil; \q their neighbors find no mercy from them.
en.R: Wicked people want to do evil. \q They show no kindness to the people around them.

fr.L: [L’]âme du méchant désire le mal ; \q son prochain ne trouve pas grâce à ses yeux.
fr.B: Le méchant a faim du mal ; \q ses voisins ne trouvent chez lui aucune pitié.
fr.R: Les méchants veulent faire le mal. \q Ils ne sont gentils avec personne autour d’eux.

decisions.choice: soul craves: the appetite longs for
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) here is desire or appetite (13:4; 13:19). A wicked person's longing is for harm, so even a neighbor gets no pity.

source.text: בַּעְנָשׁ־לֵ֭ץיֶחְכַּם־פֶּ֑תִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְ֝חָכָ֗ם יִקַּח־דָּֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: When a mocker is fined, a naive person becomes wise; and when a wise [person] is instructed, he receives knowledge.

en.L: When a mocker is punished, [the] simple become wise; \q and when a wise [person] is instructed, {{gender:they gain|he gains}} knowledge.
en.B: When a mocker is punished, the naive learn wisdom; \q when the wise are taught, they take in knowledge.
en.R: When a mocker is punished, simple people watch and learn a lesson. \q Wise people learn just by being taught.

fr.L: Quand on punit le moqueur, [le] simple devient sage ; \q et quand on instruit le sage, il acquiert la connaissance.
fr.B: Quand le moqueur est puni, le naïf apprend la sagesse ; \q quand on enseigne le sage, il reçoit la connaissance.
fr.R: Quand un moqueur est puni, ceux qui se laissent tromper regardent et apprennent une leçon. \q Les sages apprennent simplement en étant enseignés.

decisions.choice: the simple learn from the mocker's punishment, as in 19:25
decisions.reason: The mocker does not learn, but onlookers do (19:25). The wise need no punishment, only teaching (9:8–9).

decisions.choice: when a wise person is instructed
alternatives: when the simple one watches the wise, he gains knowledge
decisions.reason: The verb (haskil) can mean "to instruct" or "to pay attention"; the line may also continue with the simple person as subject, who learns by watching the wise. Either way, knowledge is gained.

decisions.choice: watch and learn a lesson
decisions.reason: Readable says how the simple learn, from seeing the punishment.

source.text: מַשְׂכִּ֣יל צַ֭דִּיק לְבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע מְסַלֵּ֖ף רְשָׁעִ֣ים לָרָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] Righteous One gives attention to [the] house of [the] wicked; he subverts [the] wicked to calamity.

en.L: [The] Righteous One takes note of [the] house of [the] wicked; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overthrows [the] wicked to ruin.
en.B: The Righteous One watches over the house of the wicked \q and throws the wicked down to ruin.
en.R: God, the Righteous One, sees what happens in the homes of the wicked. \q He brings wicked people to ruin.

fr.L: [Le] Juste observe [la] maison du méchant ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} précipite [les] méchants dans le malheur.
fr.B: Le Juste surveille la maison du méchant \q et précipite les méchants dans la ruine.
fr.R: Dieu, le Juste, voit ce qui se passe dans la maison des méchants. \q Il mène les méchants à la ruine.

decisions.choice: the Righteous One: God
alternatives: a righteous person observes the house of the wicked (and God overthrows them)
decisions.reason: The one who overthrows the wicked is most naturally God, who is called the Righteous One in Job 34:17 and Isaiah 24:16. Others take it as a righteous person who studies what happens to the wicked household, with God as the unnamed one who brings them down.

decisions.choice: God, the Righteous One
decisions.reason: Readable names God so the title is clear.

decisions.choice: "le Juste" with a capital, for God as the Righteous One
alternatives: "le juste", the righteous person, as elsewhere in these chapters
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m1 reads the Righteous One here as God; the capital shows French readers it is not "le juste" of the other proverbs.

source.text: אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] shuts his ear from [the] cry of [the] poor, also he will call out and not be answered.

en.L: Whoever shuts {{gender:their|his}} ear to [the] cry of [the] poor, \q {{gender:they|he}} too will call out and not be answered.
en.B: Whoever stops their ears to the cry of the poor \q will also call out one day and get no answer.
en.R: If you will not listen when poor people cry for help, \q no one will answer when you cry for help.

fr.L: Qui ferme son oreille au cri du pauvre, \q lui aussi criera et n’obtiendra pas de réponse.
fr.B: Celui qui se bouche les oreilles au cri du pauvre \q criera lui aussi un jour et n’obtiendra pas de réponse.
fr.R: Si tu n’écoutes pas quand les pauvres appellent au secours, \q personne ne répondra quand toi, tu appelleras au secours.

decisions.choice: measure for measure: the deaf ear meets a deaf ear
decisions.reason: The unanswered call may be to people or to God (1:28; Psalm 18:42). The law commands care for the poor (Deuteronomy 15:7–11); compare 14:31; 19:17; Matthew 25:41–45.

decisions.choice: one day
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "one day" to show the turn comes later.

source.text: מַתָּ֣ן בַּ֭סֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה־אָ֑ף וְשֹׁ֥חַד בַּ֝חֵ֗ק חֵמָ֥ה עַזָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A gift in secrecy subdues anger, and a bribe in [the] bosom, strong rage.

en.L: A gift in secret subdues anger, \q and a bribe in [the] fold of [the] robe, fierce wrath.
en.B: A gift given in secret calms anger, \q and a bribe tucked in the cloak quiets fierce rage.
en.R: A secret gift can calm someone's anger. \q A hidden bribe can cool down even great rage.

fr.L: Un cadeau en secret apaise la colère, \q et un pot-de-vin dans [le] pli [du manteau], la fureur violente.
fr.B: Un cadeau fait en secret calme la colère, \q et un pot-de-vin glissé sous le manteau apaise une fureur violente.
fr.R: Un cadeau secret peut calmer la colère de quelqu’un. \q Un pot-de-vin caché peut faire tomber même une grande fureur.

decisions.choice: a bribe in the bosom: slipped into the fold of a garment
decisions.reason: The fold of the robe served as a pocket (17:23). The saying observes how bribes work; it does not approve them (17:8, 23; 18:16; Exodus 23:8).

source.text: שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: [It is] a joy to the righteous [person] to do justice, and terror to [those who] do wickedness.

en.L: [It is a] joy to [the] righteous [when] justice [is] done, \q but terror to those who do wickedness.
en.B: When justice is done, the righteous rejoice, \q but evildoers are filled with dread.
en.R: Good people are glad when justice is done. \q But it frightens people who do evil.

fr.L: [C’est une] joie pour [le] juste [que] le droit [soit] pratiqué, \q mais [c’est] la terreur pour ceux qui commettent le mal.
fr.B: Quand justice est faite, les justes se réjouissent, \q mais les malfaiteurs sont remplis d’effroi.
fr.R: Les justes sont contents quand justice est faite. \q Mais cela fait peur à ceux qui font le mal.

decisions.choice: when justice is done
alternatives: for the righteous to do justice is a joy
decisions.reason: The infinitive "to do justice" names no doer. It may be the righteous who delight in doing right, or justice carried out by anyone, which cheers the righteous and terrifies the wicked. The contrast of joy and terror favors justice being carried out.

source.text: אָדָ֗ם תּ֭וֹעֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: A person [who] wanders from [the] way of insight will rest in [the] assembly of [the] shades.

en.L: A person who wanders from [the] way of insight \q will rest in [the] assembly of [the] dead.
en.B: Whoever strays from the path of good sense \q will come to rest in the company of the dead.
en.R: People who turn away from wisdom will end up among the dead.

fr.L: L’{{gender:être humain|homme}} qui s’égare loin du chemin du bon sens \q reposera dans [l’]assemblée des morts.
fr.B: Celui qui s’écarte du chemin du bon sens \q finira par reposer en compagnie des morts.
fr.R: Ceux qui se détournent de la sagesse finiront parmi les morts.

decisions.choice: assembly of the dead: the shades (rephaim) in the grave
decisions.reason: The rephaim are the dead in Sheol (2:18; 9:18; Isaiah 14:9). "Rest" is pointed: the wanderer finally settles down, among the dead.

source.text: אִ֣ישׁ מַ֭חְסוֹר אֹהֵ֣ב שִׂמְחָ֑ה אֹהֵ֥ב יַֽיִן־וָ֝שֶׁ֗מֶן לֹ֣א יַעֲשִֽׁיר׃

records.literal_gloss: A person of lack [will be one who] loves pleasure; [one who] loves wine and oil will not get rich.

en.L: Whoever loves pleasure [will be] a person in want; \q whoever loves wine and oil will not grow rich.
en.B: Those who love pleasure will end up poor; \q those who love wine and fine oil will never be rich.
en.R: People who live for fun will become poor. \q If you love fine wine and perfume, you will never be rich.

fr.L: Qui aime le plaisir [sera] {{gender:une personne|un homme}} dans le besoin ; \q qui aime le vin et l’huile ne s’enrichira pas.
fr.B: Ceux qui aiment le plaisir finiront pauvres ; \q ceux qui aiment le vin et l’huile fine ne seront jamais riches.
fr.R: Ceux qui ne vivent que pour s’amuser deviendront pauvres. \q Si tu aimes le bon vin et le parfum, tu ne seras jamais riche.

decisions.choice: wine and oil: the luxuries of feasting
decisions.reason: Oil for anointing the head went with wine at a feast (Psalm 23:5; 104:15; Amos 6:6). Living for such pleasures drains wealth (23:20–21).

decisions.choice: perfume
decisions.reason: Readable names the use of the oil, which was perfumed for the body, not for cooking.

source.text: כֹּ֣פֶר לַצַּדִּ֣יק רָשָׁ֑ע וְתַ֖חַת יְשָׁרִ֣ים בּוֹגֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: A ransom for the righteous [is the] wicked, and in place of [the] upright, [one who] acts treacherously.

en.L: [The] wicked [is] a ransom for [the] righteous, \q and in place of [the] upright, [comes the] treacherous.
en.B: The wicked serve as ransom for the righteous, \q and the treacherous go in place of the upright.
en.R: The trouble that might have hit good people falls on the wicked instead. \q Those who betray others suffer in place of honest people.

fr.L: [Le] méchant [est] une rançon pour [le] juste, \q et à la place des hommes droits, [vient le] traître.
fr.B: Le méchant sert de rançon pour le juste, \q et le traître prend la place des hommes droits.
fr.R: Le malheur qui aurait pu frapper les justes tombe à la place sur les méchants. \q Ceux qui trahissent les autres souffrent à la place des gens honnêtes.

decisions.choice: ransom: the wicked take the trouble the righteous escape
decisions.reason: As in 11:8, the righteous are rescued from trouble and the wicked fall into it in their place (compare Isaiah 43:3; Esther 7:10). It is not a payment for sin but a turn of fortune.

source.text: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִדְבָּ֑ר מֵאֵ֖שֶׁת מִדְיָנִ֣ים וָכָֽעַס׃

records.literal_gloss: Good to dwell in a land of wilderness more than a woman of contentions and vexation.

en.L: [It is] better to live in a desert land \q than [with] a woman of quarrels and vexation.
en.B: It is better to live in the wilderness \q than with a wife who quarrels and frets.
en.R: It is better to live alone in the desert \q than with a wife who is always arguing and angry.

fr.L: Mieux vaut habiter dans une terre déserte \q qu’[avec] une femme querelleuse et irritable.
fr.B: Mieux vaut vivre au désert \q qu’avec une épouse querelleuse et chagrine.
fr.R: Il vaut mieux vivre seul dans le désert \q qu’avec une femme qui se dispute tout le temps et se fâche.

decisions.choice: quarrels (midyanim), as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) are two spellings of the same word. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the desert: lonely and harsh, as in verse 9
decisions.reason: Verse 9 sends the man to a corner of the roof; here he goes further, to the wilderness. Vexation (kaas) is irritation or anger that she causes or shows.

source.text: אוֹצָ֤ר׀נֶחְמָ֣ד וָ֭שֶׁמֶן בִּנְוֵ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וּכְסִ֖יל אָדָ֣ם יְבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Treasure desirable and oil [are] in [the] habitation of a wise [person], and a fool of a person swallows it up.

en.L: Precious treasure and oil [are] in [the] dwelling of [the] wise, \q but a foolish person swallows it up.
en.B: Valuable treasure and oil are stored in the home of the wise, \q but a fool gulps it all down.
en.R: Wise people save good things in their homes. \q Foolish people use up everything they have.

fr.L: Trésor précieux et huile [sont] dans [la] demeure du sage, \q mais {{gender:la personne insensée|l’homme insensé}} l’engloutit.
fr.B: Un trésor précieux et de l’huile sont gardés dans la maison du sage, \q mais l’insensé avale tout.
fr.R: Les sages mettent de bonnes choses de côté chez eux. \q Les insensés dépensent tout ce qu’ils ont.

decisions.choice: swallows it up: uses up at once
decisions.reason: The wise store up (10:14); the fool consumes whatever comes in and keeps nothing (verse 17).

source.text: רֹ֭דֵף צְדָקָ֣ה וָחָ֑סֶד יִמְצָ֥א חַ֝יִּ֗ים צְדָקָ֥ה וְכָבֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] pursues righteousness and loyalty finds life, righteousness, and honor.

en.L: Whoever pursues righteousness and loyal love \q finds life, righteousness, and honor.
en.B: Whoever chases after what is right and loyal love \q finds life, vindication, and honor.
en.R: If you work hard to do what is right and to show faithful love, \q you will find life. \q You will be treated rightly, and people will honor you.

fr.L: Qui poursuit la justice et l’amour loyal \q trouve la vie, la justice et l’honneur.
fr.B: Qui court après la justice et l’amour fidèle \q trouve la vie, la justice qui lui est rendue et l’honneur.
fr.R: Si tu fais de gros efforts pour faire ce qui est juste et montrer un amour fidèle, \q tu trouveras la vie. \q Tu seras traité avec justice, et les gens t’honoreront.

decisions.choice: righteousness found: being set right, vindicated
decisions.reason: The same word (tsedaqah) is pursued and then found. What is found is the reward of right living: being in the right and treated as such (8:18; Isaiah 54:17).

decisions.choice: loyal love (hesed)
decisions.reason: Faithful kindness, as in 3:3 and 20:28.

source.text: עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A city of warriors a wise [person] goes up and brought down [the] strength of its confidence.

en.L: A wise [person] goes up [against the] city of [the] mighty \q and brings down [the] stronghold of its confidence.
en.B: A wise person can scale a city held by warriors \q and pull down the stronghold they relied on.
en.R: One wise person can capture a city full of strong soldiers. \q Wisdom can bring down the walls they trusted in.

fr.L: [Le] sage monte [contre la] ville des vaillants \q et abat [le] rempart de sa confiance.
fr.B: Un sage peut escalader une ville tenue par des guerriers \q et abattre la forteresse sur laquelle ils comptaient.
fr.R: Un seul sage peut prendre une ville pleine de soldats forts. \q La sagesse peut faire tomber les murs en qui ils avaient confiance.

decisions.choice: wisdom is stronger than might
decisions.reason: Compare 24:5–6 and Ecclesiastes 9:13–16: wisdom wins where strength fails. The stronghold of its confidence is the wall the city trusts.

source.text: שֹׁמֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו וּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֖ר מִצָּר֣וֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [One who] guards his mouth and his tongue [is] keeping from troubles his self.

en.L: Whoever guards {{gender:their|his}} mouth and {{gender:their|his}} tongue \q keeps {{gender:themselves|himself}} from troubles.
en.B: Whoever watches their mouth and tongue \q keeps themselves out of trouble.
en.R: If you are careful about what you say, \q you will stay out of trouble.

fr.L: Qui garde sa bouche et sa langue \q garde son âme des détresses.
fr.B: Celui qui surveille sa bouche et sa langue \q se garde des ennuis.
fr.R: Si tu fais attention à ce que tu dis, \q tu éviteras les ennuis.

decisions.choice: guards ... keeps: the same verb twice
decisions.reason: The verb (shamar) is used for both halves: guard your speech and you guard your life (13:3; 18:21).

source.text: זֵ֣ד יָ֭הִיר לֵ֣ץ שְׁמ֑וֹ ע֝וֹשֶׂ֗ה בְּעֶבְרַ֥ת זָדֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: An arrogant [person], proud, mocker [is] his name, acting in [an] overflowing of presumption.

en.L: [The] arrogant [and] haughty, mocker [is] {{gender:their|his}} name; \q {{gender:they act|he acts}} in [an] overflow of pride.
en.B: The proud and haughty earn the name of mocker; \q they act with boundless arrogance.
en.R: Proud and arrogant people are called mockers. \q They act as if they were better than everyone.

fr.L: [L’]arrogant [et] hautain, moqueur [est] son nom ; \q il agit dans [un] débordement d’orgueil.
fr.B: L’orgueilleux et le hautain méritent le nom de moqueur ; \q ils agissent avec une arrogance sans bornes.
fr.R: Les gens fiers et arrogants sont appelés moqueurs. \q Ils se conduisent comme s’ils valaient mieux que tout le monde.

decisions.choice: a definition of the mocker
decisions.reason: The saying names what a mocker (lets) is: one full of pride whose arrogance overflows (1:22; 9:7–8; 22:10). Pride (zadon) is presumption that sets itself above others and God (13:10).

source.text: תַּאֲוַ֣ת עָצֵ֣ל תְּמִיתֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־מֵאֲנ֖וּ יָדָ֣יו לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] desire of a sluggard kills him, because his hands refuse to work.

en.L: [The] craving of [the] sluggard kills {{gender:them|him}}, \q for {{gender:their|his}} hands refuse to work.
en.B: The lazy one's cravings will be the death of them, \q because their hands refuse to work.
en.R: Lazy people want many things, but they will not work for them. \q In the end, their wishes kill them.

fr.L: [Le] désir du paresseux le tue, \q car ses mains refusent de travailler.
fr.B: Les envies du paresseux le mènent à la mort, \q parce que ses mains refusent de travailler.
fr.R: Les paresseux veulent beaucoup de choses, mais ils ne veulent pas travailler pour les avoir. \q À la fin, leurs envies les tuent.

decisions.choice: desire that kills: longing without labor
decisions.reason: The lazy one wants but will not work (13:4; 19:24); unmet need leads to ruin and even death.

source.text: כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם הִתְאַוָּ֣ה תַאֲוָ֑ה וְצַדִּ֥יק יִ֝תֵּ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: All the day he craves a craving, and a righteous [person] gives and does not hold back.

en.L: All day long {{gender:they crave|he craves}} [more], \q but [the] righteous [person] gives and does not hold back.
en.B: All day long the lazy only crave more, \q but the righteous give without holding back.
en.R: Lazy people want more and more all day long. \q But good people give freely and do not hold anything back.

fr.L: Tout le jour il désire [toujours plus], \q mais [le] juste donne et ne retient pas.
fr.B: Tout le jour, le paresseux ne fait que désirer davantage, \q mais le juste donne sans compter.
fr.R: Les paresseux veulent toujours plus, toute la journée. \q Mais les justes donnent volontiers et ne gardent rien pour eux.

decisions.choice: he craves: the sluggard of verse 25
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it continues the sluggard of verse 25, whose endless wanting is set against the generosity of the righteous.

decisions.choice: the lazy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject carried over from verse 25.

source.text: זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־בְזִמָּ֥ה יְבִיאֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sacrifice of [the] wicked [is] an abomination; how much more when with evil intent he brings it.

en.L: [The] sacrifice of [the] wicked [is] an abomination; \q how much more when {{gender:they bring|he brings}} it with evil intent!
en.B: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable, \q and all the more when it is offered with evil intent.
en.R: The offerings of wicked people are disgusting. \q They are even worse when given as part of an evil plan.

fr.L: [Le] sacrifice des méchants [est] une abomination ; \q combien plus quand il l’apporte avec une intention mauvaise !
fr.B: Le sacrifice des méchants est détestable, \q et plus encore quand il est offert avec une mauvaise intention.
fr.R: Les offrandes des méchants sont dégoûtantes. \q Elles sont encore pires quand elles font partie d’un mauvais projet.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of the wicked, as in 15:8
decisions.reason: 15:8 says the same, adding "to the LORD". Here the further step is a sacrifice brought with evil intent (zimmah, a scheme), perhaps to win God's help for a crime or to buy him off (verse 3).

source.text: עֵד־כְּזָבִ֥ים יֹאבֵ֑ד וְאִ֥ישׁ שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗עַ לָנֶ֥צַח יְדַבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: A witness of lies will perish, and a person [who] listens to perpetuity will speak.

en.L: A lying witness will perish, \q but a person who listens will speak to [the] end.
en.B: A false witness will perish, \q but one who listens carefully will speak with lasting effect.
en.R: A witness who lies will be destroyed. \q But people who listen carefully will be heard, and their words will last.

fr.L: Le témoin menteur périra, \q mais l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} qui écoute parlera jusqu’à la fin.
fr.B: Le faux témoin périra, \q mais celui qui écoute bien parlera avec un effet durable.
fr.R: Un témoin qui ment sera détruit. \q Mais ceux qui écoutent bien seront entendus, et leurs paroles dureront.

decisions.choice: speak to the end: testimony that stands
decisions.reason: The phrase (lanetsah) is "for ever" or "to the end". The one who listens, who reports only what was truly heard, gives testimony that lasts and is not overturned, unlike the false witness (19:5, 9). It may also mean such a person will always be allowed to speak.

source.text: הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּפָנָ֑יו וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא׀יָבִ֬ין דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: A wicked person makes his face firm, and an upright [person], he considers his way.

en.L: A wicked person puts on a bold face, \q but [the] upright, {{gender:they consider|he considers}} {{gender:their|his}} way.
en.B: The wicked put on a bold face, \q but the upright give thought to the way they go.
en.R: Wicked people act tough and shameless. \q But good people think carefully about how they live.

fr.L: L’{{gender:être humain|homme}} méchant affermit son visage, \q mais [celui qui est] droit, il considère sa voie.
fr.B: Le méchant affiche un air effronté, \q mais celui qui est droit réfléchit au chemin qu’il prend.
fr.R: Les méchants font les durs et n’ont pas honte. \q Mais les gens droits réfléchissent bien à leur façon de vivre.

decisions.choice: makes his face firm: puts on a hard, shameless face
decisions.reason: As in 7:13, a hard face is brazen confidence that brushes aside conscience.

decisions.choice: considers, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: makes his way sure (the written form)
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked (qere) is "considers" (yavin); the written consonants (ketiv) read "establishes" (yakhin), "makes his way firm", answering the wicked one's firm face. Both set the upright one's steady path against the wicked one's bluster.

source.text: אֵ֣ין חָ֭כְמָה וְאֵ֣ין תְּבוּנָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין עֵ֝צָ֗ה לְנֶ֣גֶד יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: There [is] no wisdom and there [is] no understanding and there [is] no counsel against YHWH.

en.L: There [is] no wisdom and no understanding \q and no counsel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: No wisdom, no understanding, \q no plan can stand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: No amount of wisdom, understanding, or planning can succeed against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Il n’y [a] ni sagesse, ni intelligence, \q ni conseil face {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ni sagesse, ni intelligence, \q ni projet ne tient face {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Aucune sagesse, aucune intelligence, aucun projet ne peut réussir contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: against the LORD
alternatives: before the LORD (in comparison with him)
decisions.reason: The phrase (leneged) is "in front of, opposite". Human wisdom cannot oppose the LORD, nor does it compare with his (19:21; Isaiah 8:10; Job 5:12–13).

source.text: ס֗וּס מ֭וּכָן לְי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְ֝לַֽיהוָ֗ה הַתְּשׁוּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A horse [is] prepared for a day of battle, and to YHWH [belongs] the victory.

en.L: A horse [is] made ready for [the] day of battle, \q but to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belongs] the victory.
en.B: People ready the horse for the day of battle, \q yet the victory belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People get their horses ready for war. \q But only {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} can give them the victory.

fr.L: Le cheval [est] préparé pour le jour du combat, \q mais {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} [appartient] la victoire.
fr.B: On prépare le cheval pour le jour de la bataille, \q mais la victoire appartient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Les gens préparent leurs chevaux pour la guerre. \q Mais seul {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} peut leur donner la victoire.

decisions.choice: the horse: the war horse and chariot
decisions.reason: Horses were used mainly in war, drawing chariots; they stood for military power (Deuteronomy 17:16; Psalm 20:8; 33:17).

decisions.choice: victory (teshuah): deliverance, rescue
decisions.reason: The word is rescue or victory in battle (1 Samuel 11:13; Psalm 33:17). Preparation is right, but the outcome is the LORD's (16:1, 9; 19:21). A new paragraph begins here in the manuscript tradition.
